Here are photos of 2 different clones of S. rubra 'Ancestral.' The plant is found Georgia and apparently south Carolina as well, and is thought to be the ancestor of S. rubra ssp. gulfensis.


S. rubra 'Ancestral' Taylor Co, GA. This clone tends to stay small and short, but form nice clumps like S. rubra ssp. rubra:







And here's a different clone-this one can get as tall as a S. rubra ssp. gulfensis, and forms beautiful clumps:

Here are some new photos of S. rubra 'ancestral' from Taylor Co, GA. Photos were taken early December, and the plant is fully dormant. These pics will give you a better idea of what the plant looks like:

Note the beautiful, dark red coloration at the top of the trap:




It was tough getting a good shot of the entire plant because it's so 3D and my camera/photo skills are limited:
